BAGONG PILIPINAS Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http://www_dilg.gov.ph S. 2021 DILG OPINION NO. 58 MÅY22 ATTY. MAC LORD O. ZAFRA City Administrator Lungsod ng Kabankalan, Negros Occidental ocakabnkalan@gmail.com Dear Atty. Zafra: This refers to your letter dated 07 March 2024 requesting for guidance on the following queries: 1. 2. Whether the City Administrator and the City Legal Officer, who are both lawyers and thus confidential employees, may represent the City Mayor in filing a Petition for Certiorari with the Regional Trial Court against the Sangguniang Panlungsod of the City of Kabankalan to question the act of its members in passing the City's Annual Appropriation Ordinance containing certain provisions which are contrary to law and prevailing DILG Opinions? Whether the rules or guidelines prepared and signed by the Local Chief Executive implementing the programs and activities that had already been identified and funded in the Annual Appropriation Ordinance would still require the approval of the Sangguniang Panlungsod? As to the first query, we deem it proper to clarify that under Section 481(b)(3)(i) of Republic Act No. 7160 otherwise known as the "Local Government Code of 1991", as amended (LGC), the legal officer, shall represent the local qovernment unit (LGU) in all civil actions and special proceedings wherein the local qovernment unit or an official thereof in his official ca acit is a art . provided, That, in actions or proceedings where a component city or municipality is a party adverse to the provincial government or to another component city or municipality, a special legal officer may be employed to represent the adverse party. Accordingly, we are of the position that to allow the city legal officer to represent the mayor in filing a Petition for Certiorari against the Sangguniang Panlungsod members would create a conflict of interest considering that city legal officers are required to represent both the mayor, and the members of the sanggunian, in their official capacities. Evidently, this provision of the LGC not only identifies the powers and functions of a local government unit's legal officer, but also restricts, as it names, the lawyer who may represent the LGU as its counsel in court proceedings. "Matino, Mahusay, at Maaasahan" Trunkline: (02) 8876-3454

Hence, the city legal officer cannot represent the mayor in filing a Petition for Certiorari. Likewise, the City Administrator cannot represent the mayor in filing a Petition for Certiorari as the same is not one of his/her responsibilities as provided in Section 480 of the LGC. Notwithstanding, we are of the view that an appropriate course of action for the city mayor is to file administrative charges against the sangguniang panlungsod members before the Sangguniang Panlalawigan. As to the second query, our Department has consistently opined that an approved appropriations ordinance can be validly enforced so that funds corresponding thereto can already be disbursed. This is due to the fact that the effectivity of said ordinance is determined in accordance with Section 320 of the LGC, to wit: "Section 320. Effectivity of Budgets. — The ordinance enacting the annual budget shall take effect at the beginning of the ensuing calendar year. xxx The responsibility for the execution of the annual and supplemental budgets and the accountability therefor shall be vested primarily in the local chief executive concerned. " As afore quoted, the responsibility for the execution or implementation of the annual, as well as supplemental budget is vested primarily in the LCE, hence, we are of the view that when implementing the same, approval of the Sangguniang Panlungsod may no longer be required. This opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion rendered by more competent authorities and/or the courts. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY EAU ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: TTY. JU T R.
